executiveSummary: This period saw multiple high-urgency incidents spanning criminal abuse, national security misuse, and election-related risks. Notable events include large-scale AI-assisted business email compromise campaigns seeking nearly $50,000 per invoice from over one million scam emails targeting accounts payable teams View Article , persistent AI-generated child sexual abuse ads that continued to run on Meta's platforms even after removals Source , and government legal action ordering Meta to halt such ads in San Francisco Source . National security concerns escalated as Russia-linked operators reportedly used a frontier model to analyze a stolen drone vision SDK and adapt malware against detections View Article , while users in Houthi-controlled Northern Yemen allegedly sought model assistance to develop advanced missiles Source . Separately, U.S. agencies reported large-scale unauthorized extraction of billions of tokens from U.S. frontier AI models by Chinese firms View Article . Politically, Brazil's top electoral court defined "deepfakes" in ads after a campaign used an AI-generated image of Jair Bolsonaro endorsing his son Source , and Georgia election officials face pressure to remediate a voting-system issue that AI-enabled misinformation could exploit Source . Operational abuse also expanded through trusted AI platforms leveraged to deliver malware View Article , and law enforcement disrupted a criminal marketplace tied to deepfake services for scammers Source . Defensive and regulatory developments included OpenAI's provenance tooling updates (C2PA, SynthID, and verification APIs) View Article , research highlighting weaknesses in image deepfake detectors on modern content Source , and attacks undermining diffusion watermarking Source . Overall, the threat environment appears to be worsening given the diversity, scale, and operational maturity of reported misuse, despite some notable enforcement and tooling advances.

Implement finance-specific out-of-band verification for invoices and vendor changes; enforce dual-control approvals. (Analyst Recommendation)
Treat AI platform share links and hosted artifacts as untrusted; sandbox downloads, restrict script execution, and deploy content-disarm for common file types. (Analyst Recommendation)
Adopt provenance-first media pipelines (C2PA manifests, signature checks) and retain originals; avoid sole reliance on watermarking or single detectors. (Analyst Recommendation)
Prepare election rapid-response playbooks: pre-bunk common narratives, publish verification channels, and partner with platforms for expedited review. (Analyst Recommendation)
For voice threats, require call-back verification via official directories and implement known-voice challenges for sensitive requests. (Analyst Recommendation)
Monitor API usage for anomalous, high-volume, or evasive patterns; enforce rate limits and token-abuse detection with alerting. (Analyst Recommendation)
